body:
## Pull request overview

This PR implements Phase 2 UX enhancements for the console application, adding skeleton loading states, toast notifications, keyboard shortcuts, responsive sidebar behavior, breadcrumb navigation dropdowns, recent items tracking, and file upload capabilities. The PR also addresses a critical infinite render loop bug (React error #185) by fixing unstable array references in useEffect dependency arrays.

**Changes:**
- Added skeleton loading components (Grid, Dashboard, Detail) for improved perceived performance
- Integrated sonner toast library for CRUD operation feedback
- Implemented keyboard shortcuts dialog and responsive sidebar auto-collapse
- Extended DataSource interface with file upload methods and FileUploadResult type
- Added recent items tracking with localStorage persistence and sidebar display
- Enhanced breadcrumb navigation with quick-navigation dropdowns for objects

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 24 out of 25 changed files in this pull request and generated 11 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| pnpm-lock.yaml | Added sonner@^2.0.7 dependency for toast notifications |
| packages/types/src/data.ts | Defined FileUploadResult interface and uploadFile/uploadFiles methods on DataSource |
| packages/types/src/index.ts | Exported FileUploadResult type |
| packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts | Implemented uploadFile and uploadFiles methods with multipart/form-data POST |
| packages/data-objectstack/src/upload.test.ts | Added test coverage for file upload methods |
| apps/console/package.json | Added sonner dependency to console app |
| apps/console/src/components/skeletons/* | Created skeleton loading components for grid, dashboard, and detail views |
| apps/console/src/components/ConsoleToaster.tsx | Configured sonner toaster with theme integration |
| apps/console/src/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx | Keyboard shortcuts reference dialog triggered by "?" key |
| apps/console/src/hooks/useResponsiveSidebar.ts | Auto-collapses sidebar on tablet breakpoints (768-1024px) |
| apps/console/src/hooks/useRecentItems.ts | Tracks recent items with localStorage persistence |
| apps/console/src/hooks/useObjectActions.ts | Added toast notifications for delete operations |
| apps/console/src/components/AppHeader.tsx | Enhanced breadcrumbs with dropdown navigation for sibling objects |
| apps/console/src/components/AppSidebar.tsx | Integrated recent items display with Clock icon |
| apps/console/src/components/ConsoleLayout.tsx | Wrapped children with responsive sidebar hook |
| apps/console/src/components/RecordDetailView.tsx | Added skeleton loading state |
| apps/console/src/components/DashboardView.tsx | Added skeleton loading state |
| apps/console/src/App.tsx | Integrated toaster, keyboard shortcuts, and recent items tracking |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/* | Added tests for skeletons, recent items, and keyboard shortcuts |
| apps/console/src/dataSource.ts | Re-exported FileUploadResult type |
</details>


<details>
<summary>Files not reviewed (1)</summary>

* **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Language not supported
</details>

The `isMobile` variable from `useSidebar()` is destructured but never used. This suggests it was intended to be part of the logic (e.g., to prevent auto-collapse on mobile) but was forgotten. Consider either using this value in the resize logic or removing it if it's not needed.

The shortcuts use Mac-specific symbols (⌘) without cross-platform adaptation. Windows/Linux users see `⌘ K` instead of `Ctrl K`. Consider detecting the platform and showing appropriate symbols (e.g., using `navigator.platform` or `navigator.userAgentData`) to improve accessibility and UX for non-Mac users.

The `queueMicrotask` pattern here creates a brief loading flicker on every navigation. Since you set `isLoading` to `true` and then immediately schedule it to `false` in a microtask, the skeleton will flash for less than a frame. Consider either: (1) removing the skeleton if the actual component handles its own loading state, or (2) using a minimum display time (e.g., setTimeout with 200ms) to avoid disorienting flickers. The same issue exists in DashboardView.tsx.

The test assertions are too weak. All tests only check `toBeGreaterThan(0)` without verifying the actual count based on the props. For example, the test on line 26-31 sets `rows={3} columns={2}` but only checks that there are at least 3 `.border-b` elements, not that the skeleton correctly renders 3 rows with 2 columns each. Consider asserting exact counts or at least meaningful ranges to catch rendering bugs.

The `objectSiblings` array is reconstructed on every render by mapping over all objects. Since this is used in the breadcrumbs component which re-renders frequently, consider memoizing this value with `useMemo` to avoid unnecessary array allocations, especially when the `objects` array is large.

Both `uploadFile` and `uploadFiles` use the same endpoint `/api/data/{resource}/upload`. The server needs to distinguish between single and multiple file uploads, which is typically done via different field names or endpoints. Verify that the server expects both requests at the same URL and can differentiate between a single file field named 'file' vs. multiple files named 'files'.

The eslint-disable comment may be masking a real issue. The effect uses `activeApp` (line 130, 136) which is derived from the `appName` route parameter (line 57), but `activeApp` is not in the dependency array. If the app changes (e.g., navigating from /apps/crm to /apps/sales), the effect won't re-run because only `location.pathname` and `addRecentItem` are dependencies. Consider either adding `activeApp` to the dependency array or using `appName` from the location directly inside the effect.

The `onProgress` callback is defined in the upload options but never invoked. If progress tracking is not needed yet, consider removing this option from the interface to avoid confusion. If it is needed, you should use XMLHttpRequest instead of fetch to support progress events, or document that this callback is not yet implemented.

The keyboard shortcuts listed here (e.g., 'Toggle sidebar' with B, 'Create new record' with N, etc.) appear to be documentation-only — there's no implementation of these shortcuts visible in the codebase. Users who open this dialog will expect these shortcuts to work. Either implement these shortcuts or mark them as "Coming soon" / "Planned" to avoid confusion.
